event: Nala says that sounds fine, and asks what on the east road needs killing, so she goes in knowing.
"Swear first. Then you'll have all I know of it." Varne nods to the open book.
Nala lays her hand flat on the town book's page; the vellum is cool and dry under her palm.
The clerk speaks the oath a line at a time at her shoulder, and Nala says each line after him.
To keep the margrave's peace. To answer the bench's call against outlaws and beasts. To speak true.
The clerk writes her name in the book beneath a column of others, and signs beside it as witness.
Varne melts red wax onto the foot of the sheet and presses her seal into it.

changes.note: Varne seals the papers in red wax
changes.from: A sheet in Magistrate Odile Varne's small, quick hand, naming Nala Arthur a sworn hunter of Wendlow, under the margrave.
changes.to: A sheet in Magistrate Odile Varne's small, quick hand, naming Nala Arthur a sworn hunter of Wendlow, under the margrave, sealed at its foot in red wax.

event: She folds the sheet once and holds it out. "Nala Arthur, sworn hunter of Wendlow."
Nala takes the papers: one folded sheet, the red wax still warm under her thumb.

changes.note: Nala takes her sworn hunter's papers
The papers leave the bench for Nala's hand

event: "Now, the east road. My first call: rid it of what's left of Harl Voss's crew."
"The Board proved Voss and eight of his men, your work. The crew was reckoned at a dozen-odd."
"Who is left of them, and where, is the first thing I want you to find out."
"Two gold a man at the Board's rate, the same as before, head or the man himself."
"Take what time you need, but I want word before the next tax rider, ten days from now."
